Recombine 100-Day Deployments Into Continuous Long-Term Deployments

Source: R/recombine_deployment_groups.R
recombine_deployment_groups.Rd

The WildObs data curation pipeline splits long camera deployments into pieces of at most 100 days, so each piece fits inside a single-season survey (deploymentGroups). Long-term analyses (multi-season occupancy models, Living Planet Index style trends, the Threatened Species Index) want the opposite: one deployment per camera for as long as it ran without a break. This function stitches the pieces back together using the multiSeason_deploymentGroup column, which already groups consecutive surveys at a locationName that are separated by 30 days or less.

A data package goes in and a data package comes out, so every resource that carries deploymentID (deployments, covariates, observations and, if present, media) is updated together and stays joinable, and the package's temporal metadata describes the same survey groups as its data.

Usage

recombine_deployment_groups(dp, max_gap_days = 30)

Arguments

dp

A WildObs camtrap data package, as returned by wildobs_dp_download, holding at least the deployments resource. The deployments must include deploymentID, locationID, deploymentStart, deploymentEnd, deploymentGroups and multiSeason_deploymentGroup.

max_gap_days

Numeric. The longest gap, in days, allowed between one piece ending and the next starting at the same camera before the run is split into a new _partN deployment. Defaults to 30, matching the gap that separates multi-season groups.

Value

The same data package with:

  • one deployments row per continuous camera run, with deploymentGroups replaced by its multiSeason_deploymentGroup;

  • covariates collapsed to match the new deployments;

  • deploymentID remapped in observations and media, except obscured threatened-species rows (obscured_for_<category>_species), which have no camera and are kept unchanged with a message;

  • temporal metadata holding one block per multiSeason_deploymentGroup;

  • a new deployment_crosswalk resource with one row per original piece: original_deploymentID, deploymentID (the new one), original_deploymentGroups, pieceStart and pieceEnd;

  • dp$data, the in-memory copy of the tables that wildobs_dp_download adds, refreshed to match the resources.

Stops if max_gap_days is not a single non-negative number, if a required resource or column is missing, if two pieces of the same camera overlap in time, or if observations or media hold a deploymentID (other than an obscured placeholder) that is not in the deployments.

Details

100-day deployments (i.e., pieces) are chained in three steps:

  1. Pieces are grouped by locationID, multiSeason_deploymentGroup and the _CamN suffix that the camDB pipeline appends to deploymentID when one station holds several cameras in the same survey (e.g. a lured and an unlured camera).

  2. Within a group, pieces are ordered by deploymentStart. A piece starts a new chain when it begins more than max_gap_days after the previous piece ended, because the 30-day rule behind multiSeason_deploymentGroup applies to the whole locationName, so a single station can sit idle for much longer inside one group. A piece that starts before the previous one ended cannot be the same camera, so the function stops and names it; the cameras need relabelling in curation before the package can be recombined.

  3. Each chain becomes one deployment named <locationID>_ms<N>[_CamN][_partN], where N orders the multi-season groups at that station in time.

Columns are merged across the pieces of a chain as follows. A value shared by every piece is kept as is, including NA. Otherwise:

  • deploymentStart takes the earliest piece start and deploymentEnd the latest piece end;

  • numeric columns take a mean weighted by each piece's duration, rounded for integer columns;

  • logical columns are TRUE if any piece is TRUE;

  • factor columns (controlled vocabularies such as featureType) take the value that covers the most time, so they stay inside their vocabulary;

  • other date and date-time columns also take the value that covers the most time, keeping their class and time zone;

  • deploymentTags keeps each key: value pair once. Where pieces disagree on a key, placeholder values (unspecified, unknown, -, NA or empty, ignoring case) are dropped if a real value exists, then the value that covers the most time is kept, so every key appears once;

  • other character columns list the distinct values, separated by " | ".

The new deploymentStart/deploymentEnd span includes any gaps of up to max_gap_days between pieces. Calculate sampling effort from pieceStart and pieceEnd in deployment_crosswalk, not from the recombined span. observationID and eventID are left unchanged; they remain unique.

In the temporal metadata, the per-deploymentGroups blocks are replaced by one block per multiSeason_deploymentGroup. Each new block starts at the earliest start and ends at the latest end of the single-season blocks it absorbs. The package-level start, end and timeZone are left unchanged.

See also

survey_and_deployment_generator, which creates the 100-day deployments.

Author

Zachary Amir & Claude Opus 5.5

Examples

# the Woomargama project shipped with WildObsR ran four surveys over two years
dp <- example_datapackages("NSW_Woomargama_wombats_Linley_2021-22_WildObsID_0010")[[1]]
long_dp <- recombine_deployment_groups(dp)
#> NSW_Woomargama_wombats_Linley_2021-22_WildObsID_0010: 94 obscured observations row(s) kept unchanged in recombine_deployment_groups(); they have no camera to join to.

# fewer, longer deployments
nrow(frictionless::read_resource(dp, "deployments"))
#> [1] 219
nrow(frictionless::read_resource(long_dp, "deployments"))
#> [1] 57

# and every original piece, for calculating effort without the gaps
head(frictionless::read_resource(long_dp, "deployment_crosswalk"))
#> # A tibble: 6 × 5
#>   original_deploymentID  deploymentID original_deploymentG…¹ pieceStart         
#>   <chr>                  <chr>        <chr>                  <dttm>

#> 2 10_WildObsID_0010_202… 10_WildObsI… Woomargama_NP_2021_b_… 2021-10-07 03:20:43
#> 3 10_WildObsID_0010_202… 10_WildObsI… Woomargama_NP_2022_a_… 2022-01-16 02:41:54
